title: NVIDIA Corporation — Annual Report (SYNTHETIC FIXTURE for offline demo/evals)
body:
SYNTHETIC FIXTURE — This document is an invented excerpt in the style of a 10-K, bundled for offline demos and evaluation. Its figures are fictional and must not be used as financial data.

ITEM 1. BUSINESS

NVIDIA Corporation is a full-stack accelerated-computing company. Revenue for fiscal 2025 was $130.5 billion, up 114 percent from a year ago. Data Center revenue was $115.2 billion, driven by demand for Hopper and Blackwell architecture GPUs for large-scale training and inference of foundation models. Gaming revenue was $11.4 billion. The Company's CUDA software platform, with more than five million developers, remains central to its competitive position, and the Company believes the installed base of CUDA-optimised software creates significant switching costs for customers.

ITEM 1A. RISK FACTORS

United States export controls restrict the sale of the Company's most advanced data-center GPUs to China and certain other markets, and further restrictions could reduce revenue. The Company depends on a small number of foundry and packaging partners, principally Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company, for the fabrication of its products, and on limited supply of high-bandwidth memory. Customer concentration is significant: the Company's three largest direct customers together represented approximately 36 percent of total revenue in fiscal 2025, and a decision by any large cloud provider to shift workloads to internally developed accelerators could materially affect demand. The ramp of the Blackwell architecture involves complex system-level integration, and delays could affect near-term results.

ITEM 7. MANAGEMENT'S DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS OF FINANCIAL CONDITION AND RESULTS OF OPERATIONS

Gross margin for fiscal 2025 was 73.0 percent, reflecting a higher mix of data-center systems. Operating expenses grew 42 percent, primarily from compensation and infrastructure supporting research and development of next-generation architectures. The Company returned $33.7 billion to shareholders through repurchases and dividends during the fiscal year.
